2. This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C for grant of bail.

The applicant is being implicated in Crime No.170/2024, registered at police station Shivgarh,
District Ratlam (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 (2)(n) of IPC, 1860 and Section 5(l)/6, 5(j)(ii)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: Applicant is in custody since 03.06.2024.
3. As per prosecution, the allegation against the applicant is that he abducted the prosecutrix and forcefully committed rape upon her.
After lodging of the complaint, the applicant has been implicated in the present offence and has been arrested.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:26670 2 MCRC-39373-2024 innocent and has falsely been implicated in the alleged offence.
As per statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C the prosecutrix herself has gone with the applicant and both resided together for 13 days.
That apart father of the prosecutrix has filed no objection application.
The applicant is in custody since 03.06.2024 (approximately three months).
The trial will take time for its conclusion.

On these grounds, prayer for grant of bail Laxman vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48628411/
1 to the applicant has been made.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Government Advocate has opposed the bail application.

6. Learned counsel for the respondent/ complainant has submitted that the complainant has no objection in granting bail to the applicant and an application in this regard has been filed on behalf of the complainant.
7.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case as well as custody period and no objection of the prosecutrix's father, I am of the view that it is a case, in which applicant may be released on bail.

Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, bail application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant/accused be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.
It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26670 3 MCRC-39373-2024 9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
